subject: Climate & Environment
title: Melting Ice Sheets
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Melting Ice Sheets.

hook.text: Greenland's ice sheet holds enough water to raise sea levels by 7 meters.

buildup.text: It was stable for 100,000 years. Now it loses 270 billion tons of ice annually.

discovery.text: Antarctica's ice thins from below — warm ocean water melts it from underneath.

twist.text: Glaciers that took millennia to form can collapse in decades once thinning starts.

climax.text: Both ice sheets combined now add over a millimeter of sea rise every year.

punchline.text: Ice that took ages to build is vanishing in a lifetime.

quiz.question: How much could sea levels rise if Greenland's ice sheet melted entirely?

details.summary: The Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets contain enough frozen water to raise global sea levels by over 65 meters if fully melted. Both are losing ice at accelerating rates, with Greenland alone shedding roughly 270 billion tons per year since 2006.
details.whyItMatters: Ice-sheet loss is the largest uncertainty in sea-level projections. Whether collapse accelerates gradually or suddenly determines whether coastal adaptation is feasible.
takeaways: Greenland's ice sheet holds about 7 meters of sea-level rise
Antarctica holds roughly 58 meters of potential sea-level rise
Both ice sheets are losing mass faster than models predicted

faq.question: Could the entire Greenland ice sheet melt?
faq.answer: At current warming trends, Greenland's ice sheet is committed to losing significant mass over centuries. Complete melting is unlikely this century but becomes near-certain above 2 to 3 degrees of sustained warming, adding 7 meters to sea levels over millennia.

faq.question: What is marine ice sheet instability?
faq.answer: When ocean water undercuts glaciers resting on bedrock below sea level, the grounding line retreats into deeper bedrock, exposing more ice to warm water. This self-reinforcing process can accelerate ice loss far beyond what surface melting alone produces.
